one_paragraph: The commissioned primary repair is COMPLETE and verified: reader_bytes is now a real bridge-safe ceiling that never consumes a byte beyond the limit, never raises through pyreadstat's read callback, accounts exactly, and refuses loudly at the outer decode boundary, with six new negative courts proving it. The C4 closure audit is clean and, importantly, falsifiable. But the mandated R7 six-file court target of 55/55 CANNOT be met under the commissioned sparse manifest: all six files collect to exactly 55 as required, yet 6 tests fail on FileNotFoundError for two WORKER_RETURTS paths the manifest does not cover. Those same 6 failures reproduce identically at pre-candidate code in the same worktree, proving they are caused by the checkout and not by the candidate. I did not retry them away, did not expand the sparse checkout beyond the commissioned manifest, and did not edit anything to make them pass.

why_this_disposition.because: That disposition asserts the requalification succeeded. It did not: the court stands at 49/55, not 55/55. Reporting it as requalified would misstate the record.

The repair is complete and demonstrated. reader_bytes is enforced in the governed read path, bounded consumption is proved across eight ceilings, the breach is typed and prompt, and the default path is unchanged.

That is literally true of the result but misleading about the cause: it would read as a candidate defect. The failure is entirely a materialisation gap, proven candidate-independent by reproducing it at pre-candidate code.
No counterexample to the candidate was found. Zero new failures across the full 2872-test regression, and the closure audit is a clean, falsifiable negative.

The single thing preventing the mandated 55/55 is that the sparse manifest omits two governed-evidence paths the court reads. That is precisely the condition this disposition exists to report, and it is fixable by HQ with a two-path expansion rather than by any change to the candidate.

primary_repair.headline: reader_bytes is enforced in the governed read path. Across ceilings 1, 10, 64, 200, needed-1, needed, needed+1 and needed*4, bytes consumed never exceeded the ceiling. The limiter never raises through the read callback; it shortens the request and returns b'' at exhaustion, and the breach is raised as a typed READER_BYTES_LIMIT_EXCEEDED at the outer decode boundary with exact accounting.
primary_repair.additional_finding: reader_bytes was also inflated by the application's own hash and header-prefix reads, because it was read as an absolute of the whole open. It is now attributed by delta across each reader invocation, so the account matches its name and basis.
